s9.title: Einstein Level Plays at SVR F2 | FUNalysis | FRC REEFSCAPE 2025

s13.title: Page with pictures of this robot

demand.text: To be competitive on Einstein it typically aims to do every action, dropping those that conflict, such as deep and shallow climb, or are not worth the complexity and weight, such as a buddy climb.
Its kickoff scenario of about 24 teleop coral from an elite robot proved accurate; it expected more L1 specialists and missed the race for algae.

auto.text: In a Silicon Valley final a host shows three coral and an algae removal, and later calls it a feeder-station auto.

cycle.text: A full-width ground intake feeds an indexer that orients and stores coral, then feeds it to the end effector. Cameras on AprilTags position the robot to score.
In a Silicon Valley final a host shows it carrying coral while scoring algae in the processor, then scoring the coral and removing another algae.

endgame.text: Spear and fly swatter plates center the deep cage, a gearbox spools string to retract the climber, and friction from the robot's mass keeps the cage from sliding out.

changed.text: Star and flex wheels gave way to printed TPU rollers; a rolling tensioner ended, in normal use, chain skip found on the practice robot; a planned depth camera was dropped; the carriage motor went from X60 to X44 for weight; and a roller hard stop that was delaminating the side plate was removed for Worlds. The L1 bar came after the second regional.

outcome.text: 46-5-0 in official play; finalist in the Milstein division; ranked 14 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 103.23, Milstein).

facts.text: WCP X2i modules, X60 drive and X44 steer (the team site calls the modules SwerveX), free speed
Square frame side
1 x 1 tubes drop the swerve to reduce ground clearance and lower the center of gravity

solves.text: Pick up coral from any angle and miss fewer pickups

facts.text: The front roller is free to pivot, and polycarbonate wedges center the coral
TPU rollers wrapped in silicone add grip and stay light
Deploys through dual #25 chain at 65.33:1
Front rollers are 1 in and 1.25 in polycarbonate tubes with 2 in and 3 in TPU rollers pressed on, in eight 3 in segments each
Slits separate the printed wheel sections, which the team thinks adds compliance; they are printed joined by one wall and cut apart with a blade
Normal 95A TPU is recommended over the high-speed version, which came out much harder at the same rating

Silicone goes on by vacuum, a method learned from other teams, because the slits rule out the usual air method: it is pulled to the inside of a slightly larger tube, the roller slides in and the vacuum is released
Foam rollers with silicone, tried before Worlds, performed similarly but disintegrated quickly and slipped on the tube
Two to three sets of spare rollers were kept for a quick swap and never needed

cost.text: Pressing the TPU segments onto the tubes is very hard, even in 3 in lengths

functions.name: L1 bar

solves.text: Score L1 by stopping coral from going into the intake

functions.type: carbon fiber blocking bar on the intake

facts.text: Deployed by a Kraken X44 and a polycarbonate sector gear
Hooks on the bar stop the front roller pivoting up, so coral does not bounce out

solves.text: Receive, orient and store coral, and hand it off consistently

facts.text: Front star wheels turn the coral; 2 in flex wheels feed the end effector
A bent polycarbonate tray keeps handoffs consistent
An asymmetric roller layout reduces jams
A beam break triggers automatic ejection when more than one coral is taken in
All shafts geared 2:1

solves.text: Reach L4, and use momentum to score algae in the net

facts.text: Reaches full height in
Two Kraken X60 at 7:1
Two 10 lb constant-force springs counterbalance it and cut current draw
A rolling tensioner keeps the chain from skipping at high acceleration
Tensioner spring rate
A 1/4 in aluminum plate sits less than one link from the sprocket so the chain cannot skip

functions.name: Pivot
functions.type: chain-driven cantilevered pivot on the carriage

facts.text: Overall reduction 52.08:1, ending in #25 chain with a sliding tensioner
X-contact bearing supports the cantilevered end effector; inside diameter
A three-stage gearbox and a 4 in outside diameter bearing fit in a 7 x 7.5 x 2 space, unit not given
Only the end effector wires limit rotation; an elastic string shows how far it has turned

cost.text: Probably a few degrees of backlash on the final stage

functions.name: End effector

solves.text: Place coral and grab algae in quick succession

functions.type: single-motor coral and algae end effector

facts.text: One Kraken X60, 6.66:1 on the algae side and 5.55:1 on the coral side
3D printed gear and pulley combinations cut weight
Inspired by the Penn State RI3D robot
The team site adds algae pickup from the ground
About 7 lb with wires and bolts, 6.55 lb in CAD, from about 9 lb at first and 11 lb for the heaviest prototype
Weight came off by pocketing tubes and plates, 1/16 in wall tubes, one motor for both grabbers and MAXComposite SRPP in place of polycarbonate
The coral grabber holds coral from the inside, as on the Rembrandts robot, and replaced one that held it from outside

cost.text: It cannot hold coral and algae at once; coral waits in the handoff, which the team says still gave fast two-piece cycles

solves.text: Center the deep cage and lift the robot

facts.text: Weight
Time to lift the robot fully
A torsion spring deploys it after the match starts; a 25:1 MAXPlanetary spools the string
A 1 in round tube and a 0.125 in aluminum gusset touch one cage tube
The team site says dyneema rotates it in and twists the cage
Inspired by the Rusthounds RI3D design

functions.name: Pi Motel

solves.text: Fit four vision computers in a slightly smaller space than three Orange Pis took in 2024

functions.type: AprilTag cameras on four Rock 5C computers

facts.text: Cameras on the front swerve modules see the reef AprilTags
Four Rock 5C computers, powered over PCIe by a custom PCB (the team site says Orange Pis)
One camera per computer, three monochrome and one color, running PhotonVision
Each computer has its own 5 V buck converter board, capable of up to 8 A, fed through the PCIe connector
The Rock 5C has the same processor as the Orange Pi on a smaller board and takes eMMC instead of a microSD card

functions.name: Underside electronics
functions.type: electronics facing the floor behind removable panels

facts.text: Mounted this way since 2023; mechanisms on top do not block access

cost.text: Some holes in the 1/16 in panels egged out and broke after a few weeks, so gaff tape held them

decisions.choice: Printed TPU rollers on polycarbonate tube
decisions.because: perpendicular coral stuck in the gaps between flex wheels, a row with no gaps would be too heavy, and hex shafts bent in impacts
decisions.instead_of: flex wheels on 1/2 in hex shaft
decisions.cost: press fitting the segments is very hard

decisions.choice: TPU roller on top of the intake
decisions.because: star wheels picked up inconsistently in auto, which the team puts down to intermittent contact
stretch over a long chain run let it skip and the elevator lost its zero, even with an inline tensioner fully tight
decisions.instead_of: an inline tensioner alone, or heavier #35 chain

decisions.because: many teams placed coral accurately with vision alone, and the camera, its computer and a 10 ft cable added weight
decisions.instead_of: an Intel RealSense planned for field tolerance

decisions.because: aluminum tube plugs cracked around the screw holes
decisions.instead_of: aluminum plugs held by two screws

decisions.choice: Keep an X60 on the end effector
decisions.because: an X44 would overheat, because the motor is stalled for much of the match

decisions.choice: Build three robots: alpha, beta and Gamma
decisions.because: the alpha gave programming something to work with, and the beta showed design changes before the final robot was built
decisions.cost: the alpha went without intake and indexer, whose integration was too difficult; the beta weighed about 125 lb, so the main change to the final robot was cutting weight
